### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b3bc378720b16e736d3f74e4f4653afc91b55dc` — the merge of head `f3ce50a7cc2bb55ce12807ae1181253966ac26e2` into base `416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b3bc378720b16e736d3f74e4f4653afc91b55dc && git checkout 8b3bc378720b16e736d3f74e4f4653afc91b55dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad f3ce50a7cc2bb55ce12807ae1181253966ac26e2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad && git merge --no-ff f3ce50a7cc2bb55ce12807ae1181253966ac26e2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 416d9ddd3d54a0a957941a765b60ff06076984ad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f3ce50a7cc2bb55ce12807ae1181253966ac26e2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-toggle-flow-caller.pin.test.ts, .changeset/26506-toggle-flow-caller.md, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (:2552 `implements IAutomationService`, :5281-5323 `toggleFlow`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts:472, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (:1258 `Partial` host, :3010-3079 the toggle door), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts:456, the eight runtime door tests that pin the call (activation-gate-positions-name-authority, automation-activation-posture-gate, automation-body-validation, automation-packaged-base-lock, automation-toggle-deny-message, automation-toggle-unknown-flow, automation-write-capability-gate, http-dispatcher), packages/core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts (`SYSTEM_CTX`, `setActive`), packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-metadata-activation.object.ts (`systemFields: { tenant: false }`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:21513 (`userId` stamps `created_by`/`updated_by`), packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts:814, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts, packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json, docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md §5 and §7.2, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md D6.

Inputs read: card #26506 body and both comments (claim `6435538904`, os-dev report `6436156952`); #26474 body and its four comments (triage `6434156905`, claim `6434820232`, seat ruling `6434876664` letter A, amended claim `6434884699`); PR #26545 body, file list (3 paths) and the net diff of `f3ce50a7` against merge-base `3fcafcd3` (`+120 -1`, the same 3 paths); the head's check-runs, read twice (07:25:03Z and 07:29:07Z).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The widening holds at the type level, for every implementer and caller shape the brief names.** `toggleFlow?(name: string, enabled: boolean)` becomes `toggleFlow?(name, enabled, caller?: Pick of AutomationContext at 'userId')`. The member is method-shorthand on an interface, so parameter comparison is bivariant, and TypeScript treats optional and required parameters as interchangeable when comparing signatures. Therefore: (i) the only class implementer, `AutomationEngine implements IAutomationService` (engine.ts:2552), whose `toggleFlow(name, enabled)` declares two parameters, is assignable (fewer parameters is always assignable); (ii) every object literal typed `IAutomationService` or `Pick of IAutomationService` in the spec's own tests (`automation-service.test.ts:87`, `:224`, two-parameter arrows) and the runtime door's `Partial of IAutomationService` host (`domains/automation.ts:1258`, `:3078` passes two arguments) compile unchanged; (iii) a hypothetical implementation with a non-optional third parameter `caller: Pick of AutomationContext at 'userId'` is also assignable to the optional-parameter target, so the contract does not force an implementer to spell `?`; (iv) `engine.test.ts:922` (`const service: IAutomationService = engine`) still holds. The pin file proves (i), (ii) and the two-argument call by compiling them (`twoParameterToggle`, `TwoParameterService`, `twoArgumentCall`) and pins the arity as `2 | 3` and the third parameter as exactly the narrowed type `| undefined`. Nothing on `main` reads `Parameters` of `toggleFlow` with a two-tuple pin, so no existing type pin reds.

2. **The pin is compiled, not a phantom.** `packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*`, the package's `typecheck` script runs `check:test-typecheck --project tsconfig.test.json`, and the new file is absent from the shrink-only `test-typecheck-debt.json`, so its two `@ts-expect-error` lines evaluate. The reverse verification in the PR body (signature reverted, 9 tsc errors in the pin, restored) is consistent with that; I did not re-run it.

3. **The shape is right for an install-wide ledger.** `sys_metadata_activation` declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (the object file's own comment: no tenant column on this table), ADR-0131 D6 names it the tenant-less activation ledger "without D3's reserved organization column", and ADR-0126 §5 keeps the authority gate at the door with the write operator-gated there. The data engine stamps `created_by` / `updated_by` from the context's `userId` (objectql engine.ts:21513), and the runtime's `buildAutomationContext` derives `AutomationContext.userId` from `ExecutionContext.userId` (domains/automation.ts:200), so the one picked key is exactly what the write records and the same spelling `execute(flowName, context?)` already uses. A `tenantId` would carry nothing the write reads; `positions` / `permissions` would invite the second gate the engine's own docblock refuses. The TSDoc says what an absent caller means ("an absent `caller`, or one without a `userId`, means an unattributed write ... never the answer for a door that has one") and that the channel is attribution only. The two ADR citations in the TSDoc read as cited.

4. **Nothing published moves.** The diff touches three paths and no generated artifact. `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` records `IAutomationService (interface)` and `AutomationContext (interface)` by name only (the api-surface baseline records existence, not resolution); no file under `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/` or the JSON-schema manifest names `toggleFlow`; no file under `content/` names it. The wire schema `automation-api.zod.ts:814` (`POST /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle`, `ToggleFlowRequestSchema`) is unchanged, so no authorable or request shape changes. The dev's `check:generated` reading (14/14 up to date, tree clean) is consistent with what the head's tree shows; the CI `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` runs are green.

5. **The TSDoc and ADR-0126 agree on where the gate is.** The engine's `toggleFlow` docblock (engine.ts:5286-5294) says the §5 gate lives at the toggle route because it needs the caller; the new contract TSDoc says the same and adds that an implementation "neither refuses nor widens the switch" on the caller. That matches the seat ruling on #26474 (letter A, item 1: doors hand `{ ...callerContext, isSystem: true }` down and the core store writes with it instead of `SYSTEM_CTX`). The spec half leaves `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.setActive(row)` (no context parameter) untouched, which is correct for this card's file surface.

6. **File surface held exactly as claimed** (claim `6435538904`: the signature and TSDoc in `automation-service.ts`, one pin test beside it, one changeset): no edit to service-automation, core, runtime or the doors. The branch is the harness-pinned `claude/project-thread-x54rab`, as the claim recorded.

Head check-runs: read at 2026-10-27T07:29:07Z, 46 runs: 24 success, 8 skipped (opt-in and path-filtered jobs), 14 in progress, 0 failure. Green already: all six `Lint ·` jobs including ESLint, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build UI Deps`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the three claim guards, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`. Still in progress at that read: `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1-8/8)`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the landing waits for every check green.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: an optional third parameter on an optional interface method widens what a caller may pass and what an implementer may read, and narrows nothing (judgment 1). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default changes (judgment 4; the wire schema is untouched). Under the Post-Task Checklist rule a non-protocol widening ships **`patch`**, and the changeset `.changeset/26506-toggle-flow-caller.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` with both declaration lines line-initial, matching the PR body. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition marker are owed. `feat(spec):` as the changeset's title prefix with a `patch` level is consistent with the rule (the level follows the kind, not the prefix).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Carry to #26474, widening the dev's note.** The os-dev report (`6436156952`) and the PR's Acceptance notes name two runtime test files whose pins (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(FLOW, false)`) will need the caller argument once the door passes it. The head's tree has **eight** runtime test files with such pins, eighteen assertions in all: `activation-gate-positions-name-authority.test.ts:259`; `automation-activation-posture-gate.test.ts:159,168,226`; `automation-body-validation.test.ts:132,139`; `automation-packaged-base-lock.test.ts:368,399`; `automation-toggle-deny-message.test.ts:301,305` (`toHaveBeenLastCalledWith`); `automation-toggle-unknown-flow.test.ts:115,120,126,174`; `automation-write-capability-gate.test.ts:322,326,355`; `http-dispatcher.test.ts:456`. Vitest's `toHaveBeenCalledWith` matches the argument list exactly, so each reds when a third argument arrives. The server half should budget for all eight, not two. Noted for #26474's dev; nothing for this PR.

2. **Carry to #26474: a docblock on the server side goes stale at this head.** `AutomationEngine.toggleFlow`'s docblock (engine.ts:5288-5294) says the contract has "no caller channel and no room to grow one on this line". After #26545 lands that sentence is false; it is the server half's to rewrite when the engine starts reading the caller (the dev's file surface rightly excluded engine.ts). Also `flow-activation-store.ts:68` and `flow-definitions.ts:472` describe the two-argument shape; same owner.

3. **The non-human caller note needs no carrying.** `AutomationContext` declares no actor label; a service principal or agent on this channel names a `userId` or nothing. The seat ruling's item 1 hands `{ ...callerContext, isSystem: true }` down on the sibling doors, so that is already the server half's shape and no reader asks for a label today. Agreed: carrier none.

4. **Boundary held.** No `packages/spec` path was touched by the server lane (its red line), and no server path by this spec card. The claim's `Container & model: S, mode:thread, model: TIER_DEFAULT` is the dispatch's; the PR carries no governed path (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, workflows) and the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` run is green, so this record is at-tier for the schema face only.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-x54rab`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**
